questions.prompt_text:
Read the passage.

At the edge of a village stands a banyan tree so old that nobody remembers it young. Its hanging roots look like grey beards, and its trunk is too wide for five children to circle hand in hand. Before sunrise each day an old woman sweeps the ground beneath it and lights a small clay lamp at its foot. By midday it turns into a market: a potter lays out his pots among the roots, a boy sells raw mangoes from a basket, and farmers rest in the shade beside their bullocks. Parrots quarrel overhead, squirrels dart along the branches and a stray dog dozes in the cool dust. When the monsoon comes, rain drums on the leaves and children swing from the roots, laughing in the downpour. At dusk the birds return and the old woman's lamp glows in the dark. Generations have lived and grown old in its shade, and still the tree stands, quietly watching over them.

(a) Illustrate a scene from the passage.
(b) Write a poem called "A Tree" based on it.

questions.prompt_text:
Design a commemorative coin for Chandrayaan-3's successful moon landing. Draw the front and back in detail.

Some facts: India's third moon mission was launched on 14 July 2023 from Sriharikota on an LVM3 rocket. Its lander, Vikram, named after Dr Vikram Sarabhai, landed softly on 23 August 2023, making India the fourth country to soft-land on the Moon and the first near its south pole. The rover Pragyan ("wisdom") rolled out and left the Ashoka emblem and the ISRO logo printed in the lunar soil. The landing spot was named Shiv Shakti Point, and 23 August became India's National Space Day.
questions.title: A coin for Chandrayaan-3
